title: Runtime safe-mode, compatibility window, and upgrade operator
creator: Grace Liu
description: Design and implement a runtime-level 'safe-mode' + compatibility window framework and an accompanying Upgrade Operator to coordinate staged rollouts. This ticket defines policy decisions (what constitutes a breaking change vs allowed opt-in features), implements server-side guards (compatibility header, safe-mode fallback routing), and lands operator tooling to automate canary waves, client-version pings, and automatic rollback triggers based on telemetry signals.
acceptance_criteria: A stable semantic versioning policy doc describing breaking change taxonomy and a 90-day compatibility window for non-critical deprecations
Runtime exposes a Compatibility-Mode header that servers can read and honor; clients can pass 'compat=legacy' or 'compat=strict'
A 'safe-mode' toggle exists per-cluster and per-release which, when enabled, forces nonbreaking fallback behavior for known incompatibilities
Upgrade Operator can execute staged rollouts (canary waves with configurable sizes and pause conditions) and perform automatic rollback when defined SLO or consumer-impact thresholds are exceeded
Telemetry hooks emit compatibility_score and consumer_error_rate metrics; alerting runbooks reference these metrics
Migration guide and a lightweight shim-generator CLI published to docs; sample client adapter demonstrates opt-in compatibility header usage
implementation_notes: Policy: classify changes as Breaking / SoftDeprecation / Additive-only. Breaking changes require major bump or compatibility shim; SoftDeprecation uses headers + 90-day runway
Runtime: implement layer that intercepts incoming requests to surface Compatibility-Mode header and route to fallback handler when safe-mode is on
Operator: extend existing deployment controller with a RolloutPlan CRD (or equivalent) to express waves, checks, and automatic rollback predicates
Telemetry: add tags to traces with release_version, compat_mode, and consumer_client_version. Emit metrics: compat_score (0..100), per-route consumer_error_rate, token-latency-p50/p95
CLI: shim-generator reads protobuf/openapi of prior contract to create an adapter that maps old fields to new fields; include smoke tests
Docs: add migration checklist for engineers and a 'compatibility scoreboard' dashboard in console-ops
Fallbacks: prefer non-invasive fallbacks (defaults, no-op fields) and explicit flag gating for opt-in behaviour
Gate conditions: >= P0 alerts or consumer_error_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m or compat_score drop > 15 triggers rollback
comments: 2026-02-11 - Design sync: agreed to avoid introducing an API-compat header called X-Runtime-Compat; instead we will use 'Compatibility-Mode' for clarity (Grace Liu).
2026-02-18 - Security review requested: KMS usage for operator secrets; security team asked for ephemeral tokens (Miguel Torres).
2026-02-25 - Prototype demo: safe-mode toggle successfully routed 10k RPS to fallback handler without error spike in staging; observed 7% latency increase under fallback (profiling added).
2026-03-03 - PM feedback: require a 90-day deprecation window for SoftDeprecations and explicit client ping to server listing supported adapters (Ana Rodriguez).
2026-03-08 - UX review: Console integration should surface compatibility_score and a one-click pause/rollback for active rollouts (Design: Connor Martin).
2026-03-12 - Infra comment: Rollout operator will reuse token bucket quotas from Dedicated autoscaler to avoid accidental capacity oversubscribe (SRE: Aisha Patel).
